title: Personal Checking: owner asks to convert an account to Private Client Checking
content:
## Situation and business effect

This entry applies when the owner of an active Personal Checking account asks to convert that account to Private Client Checking. It governs whether the conversion is made, which decides the tier the account carries. When the conversion is made, the agent records the new tier, and the owner sees the new tier name on the account immediately; the account number, balance and history are kept. When the conversion is not made, the account keeps its current tier and nothing is written.

## Recording the conversion

A conversion is recorded with **convert_checking_tier_696add48**, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock_agent_discoverable_tool) and then called (call_agent_discoverable_tool) by the agent.

**What one call does.** One call records the named tier as the account's tier from today. Nothing else on the account changes: the balance, activity, statement cycle, overdraft election and overdraft protection link stay as they are, and no fee is posted. The tool records exactly the tier given and does not check the customer's qualification for it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Class | Meaning | Format or allowed values |
|---|---|---|---|
| checking_account_id | Id | The checking account being converted, as returned by the checking account lookup | Reference number |
| customer_id | Id | The customer reference number of the account owner, as returned by the customer profile lookup | Reference number |
| variant_name | Enum | The official full name of the tier the account becomes | Exactly one of: Access Checking, Student Checking, Everyday Checking, Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking |

## Return

A confirmation sentence naming the account reference number, its tier before the call and the tier recorded now. Receiving it means the conversion is recorded.

## Calling contract Q&A

**Q: Does the tool refuse a conversion the customer does not qualify for?**
A: No. It records exactly the tier given and does not check the customer's qualification.

**Q: Does a call change the balance, the overdraft election or the overdraft protection link?**
A: No. Only the tier changes; no fee is posted.

**Q: How is the tier name written?**
A: As the official full name, for example "Private Client Checking", not an abbreviation.

**Hypothetical call (illustrative references only):** checking_account_id "CHK-EXAMPLE", customer_id "CUST-EXAMPLE", variant_name "Private Client Checking". The receipt reads that account CHK-EXAMPLE was converted from its former tier to Private Client Checking.
